name: Rain
author: David JM
description: Background effects over the desktop wallpaper, behind your windows. Toggled from the bar: a GPU shader paints animated scenes on a full-screen background layer.

barWidget.description: A wand icon that paints animated effects over the desktop wallpaper, behind every window. Pick an effect: rain with lightning, snowfall, puddle ripples, floating dust, fireflies, falling leaves, or an aurora. Click to toggle; right-click for the effect switch plus continuous intensity and speed sliders. Effects render on a background layer behind every window, so your apps stay on top.

schema.label: Effect
schema.description: The background effect painted over the wallpaper.

schema.label: Intensity
schema.description: Continuous intensity, 1 = light to 3 = heavy. Meaning per effect: rain intensity, snow density, leaf count, firefly amount, aurora brightness, dust amount. Non-integer in practice (the slider writes e.g. 2.4); the schema type is limited to integer for the editor.

schema.label: Speed
schema.description: Continuous speed controlling the effect's motion. Non-integer in practice (the slider writes e.g. 1.02).

schema.label: Framerate
schema.description: Frames per second the effect animates at. Lower = less GPU work, choppier motion. Applies to every effect.

schema.label: Resolution
schema.description: Render scale relative to native resolution: 0.5x = a quarter of the pixels (softer, far cheaper), 1x = native, 2x = supersampled. Increments of 0.5x. Applies to every effect.

schema.label: Lightning flashes
schema.description: Rain effect: random real lightning bolts (with a soft sky flash) drawn by the shader.

schema.label: Audio reactive (Aurora)
schema.description: Aurora effect: the curtain reacts to system audio, swells with the music and shimmers faster.
